findings.title: Unintended lightness change for `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` on light themes
findings.body: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` at line 291, `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The 30% and 70% lightness values appear to be swapped compared to the rest of the PR (where `30%` maps to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`). This makes embedded post author links much lighter/fainter on light themes and darker/dimmer on dark themes than intended.

findings.title: Swapped lightness percentages for `.custom-message-length` in mobile modal
findings.body: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` at line 102, `.custom-message-length` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. In `desktop/modal.scss` (line 94), the same selector uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Having `30%` and `70%` reversed on mobile makes the character counter much darker on light themes and much brighter on dark themes instead of muted.
